prompt: In the author's protocol, why does the SCF follow the relaxation in the same folder?

options.text: ISTART = 1 reads the WAVECAR the relaxation left, so the SCF starts close to the answer
options.why: The same folder carries the wavefunctions over to the next stage.

options.text: Because VASP requires every run in one folder
options.why: Runs in separate folders work; the author keeps this pair together for the restart.

options.text: Because the SCF needs a different POTCAR
options.why: The POTCAR stays the same between the two stages.

prompt: For the optical step, the author triples NBANDS and rounds up. Why round up?

options.text: VASP wants NBANDS divisible by the number of cores (or by NCORE)
options.why: VASP itself raises NBANDS to a divisible number, so choosing one saves surprises.

options.text: Because a smaller NBANDS crashes
options.why: A smaller NBANDS gives poorer optics, not a crash.

options.text: Because the OUTCAR lists only round numbers
options.why: The OUTCAR lists whatever number VASP used.

prompt: Why can you not trust the total energy from an ICHARG = 11 run?

options.text: The potential is frozen at the SCF density, so the run only gives eigenvalues for that density
options.why: The density is not iterated, so the energy is not comparable with a self-consistent one.

options.text: Because the run uses a different POTCAR
options.why: The POTCAR does not change.

options.text: Because ICHARG = 11 uses fewer k-points
options.why: The k-points are whatever you gave, usually a path.

prompt: In OSZICAR, how do you tell that an electronic loop converged?

options.text: The last energy change is below EDIFF and the loop ended before NELM
options.why: EDIFF is the electronic threshold and NELM is the step limit.

options.text: The loop printed a line for every step
options.why: A line is printed for every step, converged or not.

options.text: The ionic step number went up
options.why: That is a different loop.

prompt: An electronic loop used all NELM steps. What does it mean?

options.text: It did not converge, and the forces from that step are not reliable
options.why: Hitting NELM means the energy change never passed EDIFF.

options.text: It converged slowly, which is fine
options.why: Slow is not the same as converged; the loop stopped at the limit.

options.text: The ionic loop converged
options.why: The two loops are separate.

prompt: A run uses 48 MPI ranks. Which KPAR value makes VASP stop?

options.text: KPAR = 5

options.why: 48 divides into 2 groups of 24 ranks.

options.why: 48 divides into 3 groups of 16 ranks; the k-points need not divide evenly.

options.text: KPAR = 4

prompt: For a large supercell, which part of each electronic step grows fastest with the number of atoms N?

options.text: Orthogonalising and diagonalising the bands, which grows about as N cubed
options.why: Bands and plane waves both grow in proportion to N, so work that pairs every band with every other band over all plane waves grows as N cubed.

options.text: The FFTs, which grow as N cubed
options.why: Tempting because FFTs are a big share of the time, but per step they grow as bands times grid points times a logarithm, about N squared log N.

options.text: Reading the POTCAR
options.why: The POTCAR is read once at the start, and its size does not depend on N.

options.text: Writing OUTCAR
options.why: Output is a tiny part of the time.

hints: How do the number of bands and the number of plane waves grow with N?
Which operation pairs every band with every other band?

visual.alt: A straight line on logarithmic axes for the cost of DFT against system size.

prompt: When is the Gamma-only build vasp_gam the right choice?

options.text: When the k-mesh contains only the Gamma point, such as a large supercell or an MD cell
options.why: At Gamma the wavefunctions can be taken real, so the build stores half the coefficients and runs faster; it works only for a Gamma-only mesh.

options.text: For any run with fewer than 10 k-points
options.why: The build can only treat the Gamma point; any other k-point needs vasp_std.

options.text: For spin-orbit coupling
options.why: Spin-orbit coupling needs the noncollinear build, vasp_ncl.

options.text: To read a WAVECAR from vasp_std faster
options.why: The builds write incompatible WAVECAR files.
